note: Synthetic examples. No real client data.

problem_statement.key_question: How can the operator cut prepaid-to-postpaid churn by a third within a year?

evidence.title: Churn drivers
evidence.content: Customers with two or more dropped-call complaints in 30 days churn at 3x the base rate.

evidence.title: Exit reasons
evidence.content: 41% of churners cite a competitor's bundled streaming offer.

options.title: Targeted network quality fixes
options.description: Prioritize cell sites driving dropped-call complaints among high-value customers.

options.title: Streaming bundle offer
options.description: Partner with a streaming service to match competitor bundles.
options.benefits: Neutralizes the most cited exit reason

recommendations.title: Launch targeted network fixes for top complaint clusters
recommendations.rationale: Complaint-heavy customers churn at 3x the base rate [EX-T1]; the calculated NPV is the higher of the two options.

recommendations.title: Pilot a streaming bundle in two regions
recommendations.rationale: 41% of churners cite competitor bundles [EX-T2]; pilot first because margin impact is uncertain.

trade_offs: Network fixes are slower but address root cause; bundles are fast but dilute margin
assumptions: Exit survey respondents are representative of all churners

problem_statement.key_question: How can the university stabilize undergraduate enrollment, down 14% in five years, without cutting academic quality?

evidence.title: Yield by aid offer
evidence.content: Admitted students offered aid packages below peer median enrolled at 18% versus 34% above the median.

evidence.title: Program interest
evidence.content: Applications to flagship programs are stable; declines are concentrated in undeclared applicants.

options.title: Rebalance financial aid toward yield-sensitive admits
options.description: Shift aid budget so offers for target segments reach peer median.
options.costs: Higher discount rate on targeted admits

options.title: Launch exploratory first-year pathway for undeclared applicants
options.description: Structured exploration program to attract undecided students.
options.benefits: Targets the segment where declines concentrate

recommendations.title: Reallocate aid to lift offers for yield-sensitive admits to peer median
recommendations.rationale: Yield is 16 points lower for below-median offers [EX-U1].

recommendations.title: Test demand for an exploratory pathway before committing budget
recommendations.rationale: Declines concentrate in undeclared applicants [EX-U2], but demand for a pathway is unverified (H3 inconclusive).

trade_offs: Aid rebalancing raises enrollment but lowers net tuition per student
assumptions: No financial model was supplied; revenue effects are directional only

problem_statement.key_question: Should the company expand into grocery retail or stay direct-to-consumer?

options.title: Run a limited grocery pilot
options.description: Place products in a small number of stores to gather sell-through data.
risks: Pilot too small to be conclusive

options.title: Stay direct-to-consumer and defer the decision
options.description: Focus on DTC while collecting market data.

recommendations.title: Do not commit to full grocery expansion yet; gather evidence through a time-boxed pilot
recommendations.rationale: No research or financial evidence was returned by the tools, so neither path can be supported. A reversible pilot produces the data needed to decide.

trade_offs: Speed of entry versus quality of decision
assumptions: All option assessments are judgment-based because no evidence was available
